_comment: Thirty encounters, ten per faction. An entry with `caravan` belongs to that caravan alone; otherwise it is drawn by any caravan of its `faction`. Entry-level `requires` gates the whole encounter (used for flag chains); choice-level `requires` gates one option. `effects` keys are resources, factions, goods, `flag`, `building`, `event`, `animals_owned` and `coin_percent`.

encounters.text: One of Merrit's horses is lame. She asks to leave it in your stable for a week, and says she is good for it.

choices.text: Buy the horse outright for 10 coin

encounters.text: Sabel Ost counts her bolts twice and comes up short. She is certain your gate hands took them, and she is wrong.

choices.text: Pay for the missing cloth to end it
"Ask Merrit about us. We kept her horse."

encounters.text: Dresk Hallow proposes a standing arrangement: a flat sum now, and his consortium passes free for the rest of the season.

choices.text: Decline; the road is the road

encounters.text: A Guild inspector wants to test your scale against hers. Yours is a little generous, which has been costing you and pleasing everyone else.

choices.text: The scale stays as it is

encounters.text: A boy on his third season asks whether the crossing needs anyone. He is not running from anything; he is just tired of the road.

choices.text: Send him on with his train

encounters.text: Half a wagon of grain has gone over. They want to tip it somewhere that is not their problem, and your ford is right there.

choices.text: Take it for the animals, cheap
Let them tip it and say nothing

encounters.text: The factor is short and asks to settle at the end of the season. Everyone at this table knows the season ends in a way nobody can see past.

choices.text: "Dresk's consortium settled in advance. You can too."

encounters.text: A Guild factor would like an assurance that a particular competitor finds the gate closed. He does not say which, yet, and is waiting to see whether he needs to.

choices.text: The gate is open to anyone who pays

encounters.text: They are running light and would rather sell grain at a loss than haul it over the pass again.
They reach the ford well after dark and want the gate opened. The road behind them is not what it was a week ago.

choices.text: Open it; the wall can take the risk

encounters.text: Assessor Pell wants to see what the crossing has taken this season. Your ledger is honest, which is not the same as flattering.
Serjeant Aud does not ask. Her four are billeted here tonight, and she expects them fed.

choices.text: Give them the palisade and nothing else

encounters.text: Rider Ilsa needs a fresh mount and will not say what the letter is. Her horse is finished.

choices.text: Sell her water and send her on

encounters.text: A clerk has been over the figures you gave Pell and found them tidy. Too tidy. He has not filed anything yet.

choices.text: Correct the record and pay the difference
Make it worth his while to lose the page

encounters.text: The muster is short and the crossing is on the list. They want one able body, and they are not fussy about which.
A levy is being collected for a bridge upriver. There has been a levy for that bridge every season for eleven years.
One of the patrol comes back alone after dark, without his coat, and asks how far the plains are.

choices.text: Feed him and let him decide

encounters.text: A writ authorises a search of the crossing for anyone travelling without papers. The Serjeant would rather you simply told her.

choices.text: "Nobody here but carters." (Cass and the Ninefold are in the yard)

encounters.text: The road east of the ford is washing out. The Crown will pay for the work if the crossing does it.
The patrol is riding east, not west, and the Serjeant will not say why. She asks what stores the crossing is holding, in a tone that is almost concern.
Old Cass asks for the lee of a wall and no questions. The Ninefold have been on the road a long time.

choices.text: Sell them water and move them along

encounters.text: Hob Ashway lays out a roll of tools. He would rather trade than be paid, and he is watching how you answer.
Wenna Fold says there are more behind her. A great many more, and they are walking day and night.

choices.text: Ask what they are running from
Say nothing and start stocking food

encounters.text: A woman travelling alone says she sets bones and asks for a bed rather than coin. She has the hands for it.

choices.text: Coin instead; the beds are for paying guests

encounters.text: Two crates, one night, no questions, and he will not say what is in them. He will say what he is paying.

choices.text: Take the coin and the crates

encounters.text: A child is sitting by the ford at first light with a name and no people attached to it. The cart she came on left before dawn.

choices.text: Hand her to the next Crown patrol

encounters.text: One of the Ninefold is back, alone, with a purse he should not have and a debt he says the crossing is owed.
A dozen on foot want to draw from the well. They are not offering to pay, and they are not asking either.

choices.text: Let them drink; there is plenty

encounters.text: A drifter who owes you nothing stops long enough to say it plainly: whatever is behind the column is not a rumour, and the ford is the only crossing for two days in either direction.

choices.text: Thank him and start counting the stores

encounters.text: Someone died on the road a mile east and the people carrying him cannot carry him further. They ask for ground.

choices.text: Give them ground and a stone
